original_question: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta and contains no cycle of length 5, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta^2?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Conjecture 28 (Mahdian), also restated in Section 6 as open problem 8.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended statement very closely: it has the right graph class (arbitrary graphs, not just bipartite or planar ones), the right forbidden configuration (no 5-cycle), the right parameter (maximum degree Δ), and the right target bound χ_s(G) ≤ Δ^2.
missing_details: Make the quantifier explicit: the statement is meant to hold for every graph G with the stated properties.
Identify Δ as Δ(G), the maximum degree of G.
Define χ_s(G) explicitly as the strong edge-chromatic number, i.e. the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring.
Define a strong edge-coloring: any two edges that are adjacent or are both adjacent to a common edge must receive distinct colors; equivalently, edges at distance at most 2 receive different colors.
Clarify that 'no cycle of length 5' means no 5-cycle at all, not merely no induced 5-cycle.
Make clear that there are no extra assumptions such as planarity, bipartiteness, girth bounds beyond excluding 5-cycles, or asymptotic restrictions on Δ.
refined_question: Is it true that every graph G with no 5-cycle satisfies χ_s(G) ≤ Δ(G)^2, where χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring of G, that is, an edge-coloring in which any two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if L(G) denotes the line graph of G, is it true that every graph G with no 5-cycle satisfies χ(L(G)^2) ≤ Δ(G)^2?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of Mahdian's Conjecture 28. In Section 4.1 the paper defines strong edge-coloring and χ_s(G), then states: 'If G is a graph with no 5-cycle, then χ_s(G) ≤ Δ^2.' The same statement is repeated in the paper's open-problems summary as item 8. So the right refinement is not to broaden or narrow the problem, but simply to make the notation self-contained by spelling out Δ(G) and the meaning of χ_s(G). The nearby context also notes that this conjecture is presented as a strengthening, in a different direction, of the earlier bipartite Δ^2-conjecture.

citations.label: Definition of strong edge-coloring and χ_s(G)
